answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, while transition mass leaks across external edges. For a sybil set S, low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S), signals a sparse boundary; min-cut transitivity bounds its probability of reaching honest volume and therefore its aggregate voting weight. A prism of attestations, a gale of fake identities, or an ocean of internal links cannot amplify influence without costly honest-edge support.
